::: {#sol-weights}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
q = torch.tensor([1.0, 0.0])
keys = torch.tensor([[2.0, 0.0], [0.0, 2.0], [1.0, 1.0]])
values = torch.tensor([10.0, 20.0, 30.0])
scores = keys @ q
weights = torch.softmax(scores, dim=0)
average = weights @ values
weight_list = weights.tolist()
print(scores, weights, average)
```

The scores are 2, 0 and 1.
The [softmax](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/multiclass-logistic-regression.html#def-softmax) turns them into the weights
`r sprintf("%.3f", py$weight_list[[1]])`,
`r sprintf("%.3f", py$weight_list[[2]])` and
`r sprintf("%.3f", py$weight_list[[3]])`,
which sum to 1.
The weighted average of the values is `r sprintf("%.2f", py$average$item())`.
The first key points the same way as the query,
so its value gets the largest weight,
and the second key is at right angles to the query,
so its value gets the smallest.

:::
